name: IT-RAT
description: Open-source governance for AI agents, and the guides that explain it.

pages.title: IT-RAT, open-source governance for AI agents
pages.description: Open-source runtime governance for AI agents: budgets, policy, memory, identity, cryptography, quality and pre-production drills. Apache-2.0, self-hosted.

pages.title: The stack: every service, with its room and its guide
pages.description: Every service in the stack, grouped by the ring it belongs to, each with a room that shows it working and a guide with the full story.

pages.title: Genaryx, the console over the stack
pages.description: Genaryx: one browser control room over the whole agent stack, on your own box. Passkey-signed kills, WireGuard-only reach and signed evidence packs.

pages.title: Guides index
pages.description: Sixteen guides: seven on the field of AI agent governance, and nine on running this stack, from a first alert to what changed in October.

pages.title: AI agent governance
pages.description: What AI agent governance means in practice: budgets, policy, identity, delegation, egress, provenance, quality, drills and an auditable record.

pages.title: FinOps for AI
pages.description: FinOps applied to LLM and agent spend: the unit of work, per-run budgets, reserve-then-settle, FOCUS showback and cost per resolved case.

pages.title: AI agent security
pages.description: The failure modes an autonomous agent introduces, the runtime guardrail that answers each one, and how to rehearse them in CI. Defensive practice.

pages.title: MCP security
pages.description: What changes when tools arrive over the Model Context Protocol: descriptions the model reads, servers nobody sanctioned, tools that change later.

pages.title: Agent identity and authentication
pages.description: Static keys are not identity. What an AI agent needs to be nameable, attributable, attestable and revocable, and when to demand a signature.

pages.title: Glossary of agent-governance terms
pages.description: Plain definitions for this field: agent passport, attestation, delegation chain, blast radius, per-run budget, rug pull, CBOM, FOCUS, drift.

pages.title: AI observability vs governance
pages.description: The record explains what an agent did, the control decides what it may do next, and both meet on one run id. What each one answers and what it cannot.

pages.title: One incident, end to end
pages.description: A single runaway agent followed through spend, policy, identity, memory, mail and evidence: what each plane sees, what it emits, and who is told.

pages.title: What runs where and what it costs
pages.description: One machine, a five-node cluster, or three clouds: the measured shapes of this stack, their throughput, and the storage line that changes by 108x.

pages.title: From zero to your first alert
pages.description: One command, one address, one mail: the shortest honest path from nothing to a governed agent that writes to you when it crosses a line.

pages.title: Two sites, one control plane, no VPN
pages.description: Sites reach one hub over outbound HTTPS through one narrow door: every site by name, one policy everywhere, and a quiet site never mistaken for a dead one.

pages.title: What is proven and what is not
pages.description: How to read a validation claim: what was measured on this stack, what the measurement does not cover, and the conclusions we published and had to withdraw.

pages.title: Three shapes of agent tooling
pages.description: The controls that answer before a call: what each one does, what it does not do yet, and how to check it.

pages.title: Security by design
pages.description: An agent can be persuaded, so its controls sit where persuasion cannot reach. Eight design decisions in the stack, and what happened when we broke each one.

pages.title: How the numbers were produced
pages.description: The eight figures on the home page: how each was measured on real infrastructure, the bugs the live runs caught, and where the rest of the record is.

pages.title: Install the stack, all of it or one service at a time
pages.description: One command for the whole stack on a box you own, a cluster or your laptop, and how each service installs and runs on its own.

pages.title: What changed in the stack, 1 to 15 October 2026
pages.description: Prices that match the bill, money that is never forgotten, tool calls judged before they run: what changed in the stack from 1 to 15 October 2026.

pages.title: Genaryx guide
pages.description: How the Genaryx console works, how Felyx is held, what every frame shows, how to take it, and what is not yet in the record, in full.

pages.title: TokenFuse guide
pages.description: How TokenFuse works, how to install and configure it, what changed from 1 to 15 October 2026, and what the default install does not do, in full.

pages.title: CostCrew guide
pages.description: How CostCrew works, how to install and configure it, what changed from 1 to 15 October 2026, and what it does not prove yet, in full.

pages.title: TokenFuse Pocket guide
pages.description: How TokenFuse Pocket is designed to work, how it differs from Heraldyx, where it sits in the stack, and why it is not wired into a running stack yet.

pages.title: Wardryx guide
pages.description: How Wardryx decides allow, deny or hold, how to run it, what changed from 1 to 15 October 2026, and what is open by default or not proven yet.

pages.title: Idryx guide
pages.description: How Idryx builds one identity graph and what its detectors look for, how to run it, what it answers, and what it does not do or prove yet.

pages.title: Scopyx guide
pages.description: How Scopyx decides an agent's web egress, how to run its two images, what changed from 1 to 15 October 2026, and what it will not do, in full.

pages.title: Vouchryx guide
pages.description: How Vouchryx proves and ends an agent's delegation, its seven endpoints, how to run and configure it, what changed in October and November 2026, and its limits.

pages.title: Qryx guide
pages.description: How Qryx finds every key and grades its post-quantum risk, the risk model, how to run it, what changed in October 2026, and what it leaves out.

pages.title: Keyryx guide
pages.description: How Keyryx signs, publishes and witnesses keys and the record, its routes, how to configure, run and verify it offline, its releases, and its limits.

pages.title: Verdryx guide
pages.description: How Verdryx turns agent spend into cost per resolved case, its six graders, how to run it offline, what changed in October 2026, and its limits.

pages.title: Typryx guide
pages.description: How Typryx works, its measured runs in full, how to choose a data mode at install, what changed, and what it does not prove yet.

pages.title: Mockryx guide
pages.description: How Mockryx fire drills work, how to run and download it, the drills added since v0.2.1, and what it does not prove yet.

pages.title: Trailryx guide
pages.description: How Trailryx proves an answer complete, how erasure leaves the chain intact, the durability runs, the offline verifier, and its limits.

pages.title: Heraldyx guide
pages.description: How Heraldyx decides what reaches a human, what its mail may carry, what its dispatch record proves, what changed from v0.7.0 to v0.9.0, and its boundaries.

pages.title: Engram guide
pages.description: How Engram works, the live runs against real Claude, how to install it, what changed in v3.0.0 and v3.1.0, and what it does not do yet, in full.

pages.title: Platform guide
pages.description: How the Agent Passport contract works, how to run the stack on a laptop, one box or a cluster, and what it does not claim, in full.

pages.title: TokenFuse, the money plane
pages.description: A drop-in gateway that gives every agent run a budget and answers 402 when it is crossed. Anthropic and OpenAI wires, proven on three clouds and on premises.

pages.title: CostCrew, the finops plane
pages.description: A crew of agents takes your cloud, SaaS and AI bill apart: allocation, chargeback, unit economics, anomalies. Nothing is published until a person stamps it.

pages.title: Vouchryx, the delegation plane
pages.description: RFC 8693 token exchange with nested act, bound to the caller's key by DPoP. A delegation an agent can prove it holds, ended early wherever the list is polled.

pages.title: Wardryx, the policy plane
pages.description: The policy plane your agents ask before acting: allow, deny or hold for a human, with signed approval tokens and a hard ceiling that outranks approvals.

pages.title: Idryx, the access plane
pages.description: One identity graph for humans, keys, service accounts and AI agents: delegation chains, blast radius, 27 deterministic detectors and a CycloneDX Agent-BOM.

pages.title: Engram, the knowledge plane
pages.description: Embeddable agent memory in one SQLite file: bitemporal facts, hybrid BM25 and vector recall, why() provenance and GDPR forget. No server, no API key to start.

pages.title: Qryx, the crypto plane
pages.description: Inventory every key, certificate and algorithm you actually run, grade the post-quantum risk against the NCSC 2028, 2031 and 2035 dates, sign the evidence.

pages.title: Keyryx, the key custody and witness plane
pages.description: Key custody and a separate witness for the agent-governance record. Custody signs for granted consumers; the witness reads the record without writing to it.

pages.title: Verdryx, the quality plane
pages.description: Cost per correctly resolved case, not cost per token: six graders, statistical drift detection and a metered LLM judge, scored on your own outcome tags.

pages.title: Mockryx, the pre-production plane
pages.description: Fire drills for your guardrails: YAML scenarios fired at a real gateway, asserting the 402, the 403 and the downstream reaction. Zero real spend, CI-native.

pages.title: Heraldyx, the alerts plane
pages.description: The part of the agent stack that writes to you: it reads the event log, decides what is worth a human tonight, and mails it with links into your console.

pages.title: Scopyx, the egress plane
pages.description: Your agents already reach the web and nothing governs it. Scopyx decides every destination before anything leaves, and keeps origins rather than URLs.

pages.title: Trailryx, the record
pages.description: A record of what your AI agents did that nobody can quietly change or shorten, where every answer says whether it is proved complete.

pages.title: Platform, the shared contract
pages.description: One agent:// passport, one event envelope, one Go binding and a Terraform provider: the contract every service in the stack shares. Apache-2.0.

pages.title: TokenFuse Pocket, the out-of-band kill switch
pages.description: Our iPhone and Apple Watch app for TokenFuse: the fleet's burn live, and a kill signed by the Secure Enclave. Built, and not wired into a running stack yet.

pages.title: Typryx, typed answers
pages.description: A typed answer, choice, score or yes/no, with a probability, never a guess: capped, journaled, and calibrated against real outcomes.
